{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZkDzoQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDKtH8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 121, "title": "Add evidence-qualified browser-local registration of original OSL text files", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `32eaf1c8763d445d7383e293bc7fdc104b4b7757`, follow `13 → 2 → OSL → 1` or category `2`. Users can list, preview and download the bundled examples, but cannot contribute a document or observation-data file.

`src/service-collections.ts` reads only bundled JSON. `src/navigation.ts` resolves READ and DOWNLOAD through those static arrays, and its `needsContent` getter excludes OSL category/item views. Consequently, adding persistence alone would not complete fresh listing, reading and acquisition.

This extends the deliberate browsing/acquisition scopes of [#59](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/59) and [#91](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/91); it is an evidenced participation omission, not a demonstrated regression from the latest mail merge.

## Expected outcome

Complete this terminal-operated journey:

`DAISIZEN → OSL → supported category → REGISTER → filename/title/purpose/body → review/edit → explicit confirmation → LIST/READ → reload or JSON restore → confirmed DOWNLOAD of the saved text`

Support original plain-text documents in category 1 and observation/tabular text in category 2. Preserve all six existing categories and the bundled files. Other categories retain their current behavior.

`REGISTER`, the composer, filename rules, limits and immediate browser-local availability are explicitly reconstructed application conventions. This increment does not establish historical DAISIZEN approval procedures or transfer protocols.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction decision

Sources were inspected on 2026-10-24:

- The [author-preserved CIARI release listing](https://cba.sakura.ne.jp/soft01/soft_pic.htm) identifies a March 17, 1996 release originally published through PC-VAN, with separate documentation, program and sample files, filenames, dates and numeric size fields. Confidence is high in the preserved contents; historical confidence is moderate to high because this is later author preservation. It supports publishing distinguishable file artifacts, but supplies no DAISIZEN registration sequence or established size units.
- The [November 27, 1998 judgment transcription](https://jucc.sakura.ne.jp/precedent/precedent-1998-11-27d.html), in its reasoning about earlier CIARI activity, explicitly identifies an OSL software-registration facility and author/user exchange. Confidence is moderate: the original judgment was not inspected and the transcription contains encoding damage. Its disputed moderation history cannot define universal SIG policy.
- The [DAISIZEN operator memorial](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/index.htm) separately lists library and OSL services, including tool and database categories. Confidence is high in its displayed distinctions; applying its undated directory to 1996 remains provisional. Retain the existing mountain-forum chronology uncertainty.
- A [1993 research paper, printed page 194](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jbes1950/44/3/44_3_184/_pdf), independently identifies a software location in PC-VAN NEC98's utility OSL. The indexed text describes registration, but PDF extraction is damaged and screenshot retrieval failed. Treat this as supplementary earlier-period evidence only.
- The [CROCUS client-author description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win31/net/se014206.html) was readable only through search excerpts. It distinguishes Quick-VAN sending from registration, which that client did not perform. This reinforces keeping registration and transfer separate; it authenticates neither host commands nor target-year availability.

The [DAISIZEN participation guide](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/sig_list.htm) remained inaccessible. Accessible alternatives support proceeding without claiming recovery of its workflow.

**Accepted tolerance:** contribution capability is sufficiently supported to implement a small local subset. Applying it to DAISIZEN is a moderate-confidence cross-SIG inference. Terminal-authored text, category restrictions, review controls, immediate publication and UTF-8 sizing are product reconstruction. Document these boundaries in existing research/About material. Do not invent historical moderation, licensing, fees, protocols or exact prompts.

### Implementation and duplication evidence

- Reuse `src/service-collections.ts`, existing navigation and the confirmed-download path in `src/commands.ts`, including its pinned payload and single-use approval.
- `src/composer.ts` provides multiline input, literal command escaping, review/edit/cancel and retry conventions. Extend or reuse only what this file-registration journey needs.
- Conference and NetNews persistence in `src/storage/schema.ts` and `src/storage/repository.ts` provide optional validated settings, transactional numbering, retry identities, author-reference checks and atomic backup restoration. Prefer the smallest equivalent OSL representation; no general upload subsystem is needed.
- Refresh OSL data through `src/main.ts`, navigation and the connection wrapper where necessary. Avoid relying on a previously loaded catalog when selecting or saving files.
- Live repository searches returned no open Issues or PRs. OSL history recovered the existing browsing and download scopes, both of which exclude uploads/contribution; no equivalent registration handoff was found. Search terminology and changing inventory limit duplicate detection.
- [PR #120](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/120) and `docs/validation.md` report final 93 focused and 473 complete-suite passing checks with three workers, including configured type checking/build. These are Coordinator records assessed by this research graph, which ran no application checks. Earlier timing/navigation reliability questions remain unresolved.

Scope excludes disk-file upload, binaries, executable content, remote transport, library editorial participation, author-management commands, AI-generated files and other service expansion.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Advertise `REGISTER` in OSL category 1 and 2 listings. Capture the selected category and existing local human author; use the existing optional registration handoff when needed. Declining registration returns safely without creating an OSL entry. Anonymous browsing/acquisition remains available. Unsupported categories and unrelated services cannot start registration.
- [ ] Collect filename, title, purpose and multiline body through the terminal. Accept a bounded ASCII basename ending in `.TXT` or `.CSV`, without paths or control characters; document the exact application limits as reconstruction. Reuse existing 200-character metadata and 20,000-character body conventions where suitable. Preserve Japanese text, spaces, blank lines and entered final newlines according to the documented composer representation. Reject blank required values and unsafe control text consistently on entry, writes and imports.
- [ ] Review shows category, filename, title, purpose, author, complete body and its UTF-8 byte count. Support metadata/body editing, HELP, explicit confirmation and cancellation. Ordinary navigation cannot silently discard or submit a draft; literal command-like body lines remain enterable. Settings/About access preserves draft and return context. Draft contents stay out of ordinary command-history persistence.
- [ ] Commit a complete entry and stable category-local number atomically. Retain bundled numbers and payloads; append authored entries without renumbering them. Reject case-insensitive filename collisions within the category, including bundled filenames, without overwriting content. Concurrent registrations allocate distinct numbers; concurrent filename collisions produce one successful registration. Failed writes roll back entries and allocation, preserve editable input and permit explicit retry. Repeated confirmation or retry after a successful commit cannot duplicate an entry, including when subsequent rendering fails.
- [ ] Store authored entries separately from fixtures using a small validated optional state. Validate category, unique IDs/numbers/filenames, allocation state, timestamps, metadata and existing human-author references. Apply equivalent checks to direct repository writes and JSON replacement. Member deletion or actor changes cannot orphan or invalidate authored entries. Preserve operational timestamps and use the existing historical-calendar presentation for displayed registration dates.
- [ ] Fresh LIST, READ and DOWNLOAD selection include persisted entries after registration, re-entry, reload, another tab's successful registration and JSON restoration. One displayed number must identify the same entry across those operations. Display safe author attribution using existing identity/name conventions; distinguish bundled fiction without inventing historical authors. Keep actual parent returns and service command scope intact.
- [ ] Acquisition uses the existing explicit confirmation path. Pin the selected authored filename and body, consume approval once, and download exactly that body as UTF-8 without BOM, with no headings, metadata or added newline. Independently verify the suggested filename, payload bytes and displayed byte count. Preserve bundled OSL and FTP acquisition behavior and truthful browser-handoff wording.
- [ ] Existing JSON export/import includes authored entries. Older backups without OSL state remain valid and produce an empty authored catalog; explicitly empty restored state stays empty. Invalid imports and quota failures leave the previous world intact. Reset removes authored entries through existing confirmation semantics. World replacement invalidates pending registration and acquisition, including across awaited operations; stale drafts cannot save into the replacement world. Browsing and cancellation create no OSL state. Explicit human registration and ordinary session/history bookkeeping retain their existing behavior.
- [ ] Keep OSL entries outside forum/mail/conference/OLT/NetNews collections and resident-generation context. With automatic activity paused, compare protected records before/after successful registration and non-writing journeys, allowing only the intended OSL state and legitimate existing registration/session changes. Preserve consent, scheduling, empty-world and storage safeguards. No model, inference or external connection is required.
- [ ] Extend existing Playwright/controller/repository coverage using `tests/osl-download.spec.ts`, service tests and conference/NetNews transaction/restore patterns. Cover both supported categories, review/edit/cancel, literal Japanese/markup/command text, collisions, concurrent allocation, rollback/retry, author-reference validation, legacy/empty/invalid restoration, stale-world invalidation and exact downloads. Include production keyboard journeys through registration → reload/restore → acquisition, simulated IME Enter protection, Settings return and usable input/scrolling at 320px. Preserve existing functional, storage, consent, composition and terminal pacing/skip regression coverage.
- [ ] Update README usage, existing About/Details, backup descriptions and `docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md`, replacing affected bundled-only/no-contribution claims precisely. Record source URLs, inspection dates, historical scope, confidence, inaccessible references and reconstruction assumptions. Keep routine service output concise Japanese and provenance available on demand.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs the documented `npm test` workflow before merge; `npm test -- --workers=3` is acceptable with the actual worker setting disclosed. Existing configuration performs TypeScript checking and production bundling. Review the complete diff, check affected documentation links and run `git diff --check`. Record actual results, failures and skipped checks; introduce no unrelated framework.

## Optional validation

Additional dated OSL manuals/session logs may refine registration, approval and transfer distinctions. Native IME observation, other browser engines and historical-user feedback are optional refinements, not completion gates. Real-model generation is unnecessary.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge.
